messages:
Maria Chen: heads up — after tuning emit window down to 30ms on r10 canary I'm seeing p95 regressions for short responses (~2-6 tokens). Not huge throughput change but perceived latency feels worse :eyes:
Ashok Patel: can you paste the canary config and the kernel selection logs? any fallback to slower kernels?
Maria Chen: config snippet: ```emit_chunk_ms: 30
microbatch_max_tokens: 64
microbatch_target: 6
kv_cache_prefetch: true
kernel_pref_threshold: 0.75```
Maria Chen: logs show repeated kernel fallback on q4_0->f32 path for sequences with many prompt prefixes; kernel_selector: "chosen=fast_attn_v2" then quickly "fallback=gemm_fallback" for some batches.
Ben Ortiz: interesting. fallback frequency? that would blow up tail if fallback is non-preemptible and blocks other batches.
Maria Chen: ~6% of microbatches on the canary, but those microbatches are the ones with many short responses (lots of small emits). p99 not much change but p95 shifts up ~40ms.
Ashok Patel: small emits create more kernel churn + smaller matmul sizes; combined with emit flush -> more context switches on the runtimes. Could be scheduling thrash.
Lucy (ci-bot): perf-dashboard link: https://perf.redwood.internal/dashboards/emit-window-canary/1971 (canary id 1971) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Ben Ortiz: can we repro locally with the same microbatch sizing and a synthetic prompt distribution? I want to trace NVTX around the fallback region.
Maria Chen: repro script attached inline: ```python
# synth_repro.py (very small)
from runner import Client
cli = Client(model="redwood-open-q4_0")
for _ in range(1000):
    prompt = "Tell me a 3-word summary of X"
    cli.stream(prompt, emit_chunk_ms=30, max_tokens=6)
```
Maria Chen: NVTX shows that gemm_fallback takes ~2.8ms vs fast_attn_v2 ~0.9ms at these sizes. But the issue is that fallbacks are not being scheduled to overlap well with other microbatches; they push other emits behind.
Ashok Patel: two axes to try: 1) increase emit_chunk_ms slightly (to 50ms) to allow more coalescing, 2) change kernel_pref_threshold to prefer fast_attn unless very cheap. Both are cheap experiments.
Ben Ortiz: also consider increasing microbatch_target so that each kernel run has enough work to stay in fast path. e.g. target 10 tokens/batch. That will reduce delta between kernels.
Maria Chen: tried target=10 in canary (commit 8ab23f0 rollback experiment) — p95 improved back to baseline but throughput dropped ~4% for long queries. tradeoff looks classic: perceived latency down, bulk throughput down.
ops-bot: note: canary 1971 recorded commit 8ab23f0, rollback tag applied by @maria at 1971234580
Maria Chen: also found KV cache behavior odd: prefetching true + small emits causes more KV reads per emit; on some sequences KV cache misses trigger extra compute before kernel selection, slightly delaying the fast_attn path.
Ashok Patel: could we add a cheap heuristic: if upcoming response length <= X and KV cache miss rate > Y, temporarily bump emit window to allow KV warmup?
Ben Ortiz: yea, or do a two-stage emit: immediate tiny emit for first char(s) then hold a slightly larger chunk for the rest (per-connection smoothing). Might be hairy.
Maria Chen: idea: per-route smoothing config that adjusts emit_chunk_ms based on rolling tail percentiles and kernel fallback rate. If fallback > 3% then bump emit_chunk_ms by +20ms for that route.
Ashok Patel: that feels reasonable and local — implement as part of the scheduling policy rather than changing global defaults. We can A/B it.
Lucy (ci-bot): created issue PERF-3142: rollout per-route emit smoothing + kernel-fallback metric.
Maria Chen: next steps: 1) A/B canary with per-route smoothing, 2) temp bump kernel_pref_threshold in canary to reduce fallback, 3) monitor p95/p99 and throughput. I'll push a small change to the scheduler tomorrow.
Ben Ortiz: add NVTX traces to the canary so we can see overlap. Also snapshot kernel selection histogram per microbatch size.
Ashok Patel: I'll simulate a mixed workload in perf lab (short + long replies) and run grid over emit_chunk_ms in {30,40,50,60} x microbatch_target {6,8,10,12}.
Maria Chen: thanks — I think the key takeaway: tiny emit window reduces single-response latency in isolation but increases kernel churn + KV miss surface, hurting perceived p95 under mixed workloads. Need smoothing + fallback-aware heuristics. :thumbsup:
